rationale: The NP benchmark (Prolangs-C++) is a small, record- and string-oriented C++ program with many short functions and negligible compute-hot loops, so low-cost, high-assurance passes should dominate. SUB is weighted highest on every dimension because instruction substitution is cheap in both size and time, essentially correctness-safe, and directly hardens the string/integer comparisons this program relies on; SPLIT likewise gets high weights since it is nearly free and amplifies the effectiveness of the other transforms. IBR and ICALL receive strong SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights with tolerant cost weights because indirect branching and calls are inexpensive at runtime and obscure control flow in many-small-function code. BCF gets high SecurityGain but low RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so the bogus-control-flow pass is reserved only for functions whose features indicate genuinely low cost and high gain, avoiding its typical size blowup across many tiny functions; FLA is similar but even more restrained since flattening pays off mainly in larger loop-containing functions, which NP largely lacks. IGV keeps moderate weights to gain diversity from global-variable hiding at acceptable size cost. Overall the table biases selection toward cheap, safe, diversity-adding transforms everywhere while gating the expensive bloating passes behind strict cost/gain feature thresholds, maximizing resistance with bounded overhead and correctness risk.
